title: Clustering: k-means, DBSCAN and hierarchical — and how to read the result

videos.script: Nobody has ever labelled a customer as a kind of customer. {{nobody}} The marketing team wants kinds anyway, one newsletter each. {{kinds}} This is learning without an answer to check against. {{unsupervised}} k-means puts each customer with the nearest of a few centres. {{kmeans}} Forget to scale the columns, and the size of a basket decides everything. {{scale}} Then how many groups. Two measurements agree on four, which is rarer than it sounds. {{four}} DBSCAN finds the groups by density, and leaves a few customers out. {{dbscan}} A tree of merges finds them again. {{tree}} And the test that stands in for a label: refit on half the customers, and see whether the same groups come back. {{stable}} By the end, a cluster is something you can describe, defend and test, not just draw. {{end}}
